summary: Local ancestry attribution observes effective UID before reading ancestor environments. A positively observed ownership transition ends the cooperative walk as a person, preserving ordinary login-shell and SSH requests. Same-UID inspection failures and unknown ownership remain unverifiable.

compatibility.detail: Linux reads effective UID from process status; macOS uses shared PROC_PIDTBSDINFO parent/birth/UID metadata, with PROC_PIDT_SHORTBSDINFO as an owner-only observation when full metadata is refused. Owner-only metadata never supplies a generation witness. Present empty, conflicting or invalid identity values still refuse sensitive requests. macOS has no pidfd: before/after birth checks narrow but cannot eliminate the PID reuse window. Ancestry binding prevents accidental impersonation by cooperative agents; it is not a boundary against deliberate evasion. See schickling/dotfiles#8659.

recovery.detail: Revert the commit and restart the daemon.
